does: Holds the Architecture part of stage 02: reads the statement of a job and the organization's stack, and writes the architecture record, naming the systems the agent reaches in plain words, binding a product to each in dev, test and production (the organization's choice first, the platform's default for the rest), and recording its dependencies, kind, limits, egress, formats, settings and every decision with its reason. Asks what only a person can commit to, and designs nothing.

offerings.name: Write the architecture
offerings.does: Writes the architecture record for an agent from the statement of its job, and names what it could not settle.

inputs.name: the statement of the job
inputs.about: What the agent is for, in the words of whoever wants it, however untidy: the Requirements stage's statement. Plain words or Markdown, in the message itself or attached as a file.

inputs.name: the organization's stack
inputs.about: The stack section of the organization record (AgentMesh docs/account-stack.md), `{bindings, production_stands_in?}`: one binding per system, each with its product, who provides it and a row per environment. Exact typed data the binding step reads; credentials and addresses in it are never copied into the record.

inputs.name: the platform's defaults
inputs.about: The reserved system names with the House Stack's product on each, as GET /v1/stack/vocabulary answers, `{systems}`. Absent, the copy this package carries is used and the reply says so.

outputs.name: the architecture record
outputs.about: Markdown: a front matter header `record, statement, environments, kind, done, questions, systems, bindings`, then `## Statement`, `## Systems`, `## Bindings`, `## Dependencies`, `## Kind`, `## Limits`, `## Egress`, `## Formats`, `## Settings`, `## Decisions` and `## Questions`. The header's bindings give the product and who provides it for each system in each environment, for the Design and a test to read.

outputs.name: what is still open
outputs.about: Markdown: a front matter header `record, questions`, then `## Questions` with one line per question under its key, then `## How to answer`. Delivered only when a question is open.

steps.name: Read what was asked
steps.does: Records the statement, the organization's stack, the platform's defaults and any earlier record, tells a revision from a new request and a request this role does not do from one it does, and judges nothing else.

steps.name: Name the systems
steps.does: Calls the text-reasoning service once, twice at most, to read the statement and name the systems, the capability each model system needs, the kind, the dependencies, the limits, the egress, the formats and each decision with its reason; then puts right in code what a record must never carry and asks every commitment the answer filled in.

steps.name: Bind each environment
steps.does: Binds each system in each environment from the organization's stack first and the House Stack for the rest, in the order the deploy's own resolver walks, and asks wherever neither may stand.

steps.name: Check the record
steps.does: Writes the record and holds it to the Architecture part's done-when: every system named and bound in each environment, every decision with its reason, no model name, address or credential; in a revision it also writes what changed.

steps.name: Write the reply
steps.does: Writes the reply, with the questions nobody else could answer, and files the pieces.

offerings.name: Revise the architecture
offerings.does: Revises an architecture record with the person's answers or what to change, keeps the rest, and lists the lines that changed with the reason for each changed decision.

inputs.name: the record to revise
inputs.about: An architecture record this role wrote: Markdown with a front matter header `record, statement, environments, kind, done, questions, systems, bindings`. Absent, the newest record an earlier job wrote is revised.

inputs.name: what to change
inputs.about: What to change, in words: a correction, a new fact, or a design step that needs something the record does not name, which is asked as a question and never added on the designer's word.

inputs.name: answers to its questions
inputs.about: One line per answer, `key: answer`, under the key each open question names (limit-cost, egress-1, binding-<system>-<environment>, system-<name>).

refusals:
Writing the statement of the job. The statement is the Requirements stage's and the person's own words; an architecture written from a statement this agent invented answers a job nobody asked for. It is declined, and the reply asks for the statement.
Designing the steps or writing the spec. The Design is held by the spec writer for an agent and the solution planner for a solution, and it designs within the record; a record that also designed would be checked by nobody. It is declined, and the reply says who holds it.
Choosing the agent that does a step. That is the Source stage's, held by the catalog. It is declined, and the reply says so.
Naming a system by its product, an address or an account. A system is named in plain system words and the product is the binding, so a package that works for one organization's stack works for another's; a system named by its product is renamed in code to its system.
Binding a platform default where the organization chose a product. The organization's choice is the binding wherever it made one; a default fills only what it left open, and is marked as a default.
Filling in a commitment. A spending limit, a product neither the organization chose nor the platform offers, access to a system the statement does not call for and a network destination beyond the derived set are commitments somebody would be held to, so each is asked, and any the model filled in is taken back out in code.
Adding a system on a designer's word. A design step that needs a system the record does not name comes back as a question for the person, and the record is revised only with their answer.
Putting a model's name, an address or a credential into a record. A model is the text-reasoning binding's, placed at install; an address and a credential are what the owner's instruction supplies at Deploy. Each is taken out of the answer in code, and a record that still carries one is not delivered.
Delivering a record as finished while a question is open. The record goes, so the person can read it and answer, and its header says done: no.
Asking a third time. The architecture is asked for, checked and asked once more with the findings, and then it stands with the findings named.
escalates: A binding that cannot be made, a spending limit, a destination beyond the derived set, or a system the statement does not call for. None of them can be read off a statement, and each is a commitment somebody would be held to.
An architecture that still carries findings after two goes. It is delivered with the findings named, and what to do about it is the person's decision.

records.name: the request as it arrived: the statement, the stack, the defaults, any earlier record and the answers, per job
the checked architecture before binding, the questions it raised and what code put right, per job
each system's binding in each environment, where it came from, and the questions where none could stand
whether the record is done, every reason it is not, and the record's digest
how many calls were made to the text-reasoning service and which model answered
what this job did not have and did anyway: each thing that was missing, what was done instead, and the reason where it is known
the signed job manifest of each delivery, listing each piece by the step that made it. The adapter signs it from pieces.json and keeps it beside the reply.
